name: עֵינָן
summary: Enan of Naphtali is known only as the father of Ahira, his tribe's leader in the wilderness, who brought Naphtali's offering and led its army when Israel set out from Sinai (Num 1:15; 2:29; 7:78, 83; 10:27). The name is עַיִן with the ending ‑ān. The same form ends the place name Hazar-enan on Israel's northern border (Num 34:9–10), and a Targum gives עֵינָן for the place הָעַיִן, “the spring”, in Num 34:11; so the name most likely means “of springs”. Since עַיִן is the eye as well, “of eyes, keen-sighted” cannot be ruled out.

evidence.note: Over the army of the tribe of Naphtali, Ahira son of Enan.
חֲצַר עֵינָן, the same form in a place name on the northern border.
The border runs east of הָעַיִן, “the spring”, a place.
Targ. Y. I Num 34:11 has עֵינָן where the Hebrew has עַיִן (Targ. Y. II עינותא).
The root's noun: עֵין הַמַּיִם, a spring of water.

note: BDB key p.ck.aq gathers eight tokens: five of the man (Num 1:15; 2:29; 7:78, 83; 10:27) and three of Hazar-enan (Num 34:9, 10; Ezk 48:1) filed by spelling; Hazar-enan is a place and has no entry. Which of “spring” or “eye” the name intends is not settled by any verse.
